headline: Union play behind closed doors in Düsseldorf — and stay clear favourites
summary: Union St. Gilloise's Europa League tie with Hapoel Beer Sheva will be played behind closed doors in Düsseldorf: Leuven's mayor banned the game and Union's own ground does not meet UEFA rules. The crowd is gone; the favouritism is not. David Hubert's side have not lost since mid-September, and last week Beer Sheva lost 1-2 at AZ Alkmaar, giving up 2.75 expected goals. Belgian media report three important Union players are back. Union are 71.1% to win and Beer Sheva 11.8%; the market gives Beer Sheva a head start of 1.5 goals. The fair goals total is 3.14.
read: Union St. Gilloise are clear favourites: unbeaten in five, four points from two Europa League games and far the better chance numbers, against a Beer Sheva side with one point and a 1-2 defeat at AZ behind them. The tie is being played behind closed doors in Düsseldorf, so the 'home' advantage is nominal, and the market expects roughly three goals with Union rated about a goal and a half the stronger side.

facts.fact: The match is being played behind closed doors in Düsseldorf: Leuven's mayor banned the game at Den Dreef for geopolitical reasons and Union's Stade Marien does not meet UEFA regulations.
facts.meaning: Union lose any real home advantage — an empty neutral stadium for a game they are heavy favourites in.

facts.fact: Union St. Gilloise are 71.1% to win, more than six times Beer Sheva's 11.8%.
facts.meaning: This is a lopsided tie on paper — Union are more likely than not to win, and comfortably.

facts.fact: Union are unbeaten in their last five across all competitions — three wins, two draws.
facts.meaning: They arrive with rhythm, four days after their last outing.

facts.fact: Union out-created Real Sociedad 1.92 xG to 0.76 and still only drew 1-1 in their last Europa League game.
facts.meaning: The chance quality is there against good opposition; the scoreline undersold them.

facts.fact: The market's fair handicap line is Union -1.54, with the main line at -1.5.
facts.meaning: The market rates Union about a goal and a half better; they need to win by two for the -1.5 handicap to land, which is roughly a coin flip.

facts.fact: The market's fair total is 3.14 goals, with the under marginally favoured at the 3.25 line.
facts.meaning: A high-scoring game is expected, but the price leans just under three and a quarter goals.

facts.fact: Beer Sheva lost 1-2 at AZ Alkmaar last week and gave up 2.75 xG in the process.
facts.meaning: Away from home their defence has been the weak point, and this tie gives them no home comforts either.

facts.fact: Union are without defender K. Mac Allister, who has played 638 minutes this season at a 7.3 rating.
facts.meaning: A first-choice defender missing from a side that has conceded twice in its last five games.

sources.fact: The match is being played behind closed doors in Düsseldorf, with Union Saint-Gilloise unable to host at Den Dreef in Leuven because the mayor banned the game there for geopolitical reasons and the Stade Marien does not meet UEFA regulations.
Both Union Saint-Gilloise and Beer-Sheva lament having to play the Europa League match behind closed doors, with a club figure quoted saying 'It's really annoying. Football is for the fans.'
Union Saint-Gilloise recover three important players for the Europa League match against Hapoel Beer-Sheva in Düsseldorf.
Le Soir reports that Union Saint-Gilloise trained in Düsseldorf on Wednesday evening on the eve of their match against Hapoel Beer-Sheva and have notable players returning.
Union Saint-Gilloise are coached by David Hubert.
Union Saint-Gilloise have won four of their last five matches across all competitions.
Union Saint-Gilloise were missing 10 players for their earlier Europa League home game against Real Sociedad.
Union Saint-Gilloise's most recent success mentioned in the preview was a 3-0 win.
